newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures up on lower stocks, frigid weather.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures up on lower stocks, frigid weather.

text.p: IPE oil futures built on their morning gains in fairly volatile trade on Wednesday as continued cold weather insulated the market from any short-term downward pressure, traders said.
Dec gas oil was trading up $3.25 at $225.00 a tonne at 1540 GMT in fairly light volume, while Jan Brent was up 25 cents at $23.63.
Jan Brent repeatedly fluctuated around $23.60, and seemed to have breached that resistance level, traders said.
"It think it's heading to $24.00 by the end of the week," one trader said.

Both gas oil and crude futures rallied following the latest Energy Information Administration figures, which showed a smaller drop in crude stocks than the API had reported on Tuesday and a drop in distillate stocks rather than an increase.
"It's seasonal, but in the right direction," the trader said. "No one wants to be caught short."

The EIA reported that U.S. distillate stocks fell 900,000 barrels to 113.2 million barrels in the week to November 15, while crude oil stocks (excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve) fell 2.4 million barrels to 305 million barrels.
Gas oil trade remained light and traders said the market continued to await the outcome of where the 865,100 tonnes of physical gas oil to be delivered into the November contract would end up.
"If it hits the market, it will have a real impact," another trader said.
The IPE said it was closely monitoring the situation.
Cold weather was the crucial factor behind the market's rise, traders said. Weather Services Corp has forecast frigid weather across the United States to continue through the weekend.
